BBC News — confirmed published 1 October 2026, 15:38 GMT (16:38 BST), updated through the evening (RSS pubDate 18:48 GMT / 19:48 BST).
Headline: "Netanyahu says flight attacker 'underwent Islamist radical indoctrination'"

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says investigations suggest the man who stabbed his fellow pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".

Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu also said it was looking "very likely" that the attacker, who he said was an Omani national, "was going to down the plane".

The co-pilot is currently being questioned in Saudi Arabia, where the plane made an emergency landing. However UAE officials say they have jurisdiction over the incident because the aircraft is registered there and flies under its flag.

QUOTE (Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, to Fox News): once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal that's not a question".

QUOTE (Benjamin Netanyahu): "And with all the passengers in there, and if you couple that with what I just told you about the Islamist tendencies, that radicalisation that were found in his background, I think ... that'll give us a pretty good clue but again I don't make final conclusions yet but that's the indications we have now."

Preliminary findings from a separate Israeli investigation suggest the alleged attacker intended to crash the plane, an Israeli security source told BBC Arabic.
